description: EchoTrace (Cairo) explores how NASA NISAR radar sees a mixed agricultural and urban area change over time. Using 24 real radar passes over a 16x16 km area in Punjab, India (324 days, Nov 2025 - Oct 2026), our interactive app lets visitors act as data detectives: pick a spot, browse every date, read the evidence, and weigh competing explanations. We state what the data shows and what stays a hypothesis.
summary: EchoTrace built Change Courtroom: Punjab fields, an interactive investigation space on real NASA NISAR L2 GCOV radar data. It follows 24 radar passes over a 16x16 km mixed agricultural and urban area in Punjab, India (21 Nov 2025 - 11 Oct 2026), tracking HH and HV backscatter per pixel. Visitors act as data detectives: pick one of 12 candidate change areas, browse deviation maps for every date, read per-area time series, and weigh competing explanations against the documented crop calendar from Punjab Agricultural University. The app states what the data shows and what stays a hypothesis, and shows its selection rule so visitors can judge it. Every number is computed from the 24 NASA granules listed inside, accessed via ASF DAAC. Built to make radar change readable to non-specialists.
details: Change Courtroom: Punjab fields is an interactive web app that turns 324 days of NASA NISAR radar observations into an investigation space. Visitors choose one of 12 candidate change areas, browse deviation maps for 24 acquisition dates, read HH/HV time series, and weigh competing explanations against the measured data and documented regional crop-calendar context. How it works: 24 NISAR L2 GCOV granules from 21 November 2025 to 11 October 2026 were accessed via NASA's ASF DAAC. They cover a 16x16 km mixed agricultural and urban area in Punjab, India, on a 10 m grid. Gamma0 power is converted to dB and compared with each pixel's temporal median. The exploratory selection rule flags changes greater than 3 dB on at least 4 dates in each channel, not necessarily the same dates. The 12 displayed areas are selected examples, not proven anomalies. All 24 granule identifiers are listed inside the app. Tools: Python, h5py and NumPy for data extraction; React and TypeScript for the app. Punjab Agricultural University and ICAR publications provide regional agricultural context, not field-level validation. The intended benefit is to help non-specialists ask what changed and when, with evidence and uncertainty visible together. Plain-language definitions, guided entry questions and worked examples support this data-detective approach. Limits: the analysis uses no land-cover mask or independent field validation. Radar changes can reflect moisture, vegetation, roughness and other factors, so we do not claim crop classification or proven causes. The data has PROVISIONAL maturity. Four expected acquisition cycles have no matching catalog scene, including one within the documented instrument gap. Original cluster-grouping parameters were not archived, so the exact cluster selection is not fully reproducible. The app and current source archive do not constitute a fully reproducible open-source release.
